bullets: Certified Shift Concussion management framework
One-on-one appointments focused on explanation, education, and reassurance
Targeted exercises for neck stiffness and dizziness triggers
Evidence-based strategies for gradual screen and reading tolerance
customSections.content: A concussion is a mild traumatic brain injury caused by a force to the head or body that disrupts how brain systems function. Without guidance, many people fall into one of two traps: pushing too hard and flaring symptoms, or avoiding activity altogether out of fear. Both prolong recovery. At our Calgary clinic, we evaluate your vision, balance, neck movement, and activity tolerance to establish a safe, progressive recovery plan.
customSections.imageAlt: Concussion rehabilitation at Nose Creek Physiotherapy Calgary
customSections.subtitle: Why rest alone is not enough — safe, structured progression tailored to you.

faqs.answer: While many concussions resolve within 2 to 4 weeks with proper guided care, some individuals experience symptoms that last for months. Recovery is rarely a straight line. Structured assessment under the Shift Concussion framework helps identify specific visual, balance, or neck impairments and prevents symptoms from becoming chronic.
faqs.question: How Long Do Concussion Symptoms Usually Last?

faqs.answer: Yes, under clinical supervision. Complete dark-room rest is no longer recommended by concussion science. Sub-symptom threshold exercise (such as light stationary cycling or walking) increases cerebral blood flow and speeds recovery, provided you stay below the threshold that flares your symptoms.
faqs.question: Can I Exercise If I Still Have Concussion Symptoms?

faqs.answer: Yes, symptom fluctuation is completely normal. Factors like poor sleep, cognitive load at school or work, screen exposure, or physical fatigue can temporarily elevate symptoms. Our clinic teaches pacing strategies to help you navigate these daily fluctuations.
faqs.question: Is It Normal for Symptoms to Change Day to Day?

faqs.answer: If symptoms spike, it usually indicates that an activity exceeded your current neurological or physical threshold. This is a normal part of recovery. We simply adjust your activity pacing, treat any cervical neck restrictions, and gradually re-advance your boundaries.
faqs.question: What Happens If Concussion Symptoms Return After Improvement?

faqs.answer: You do not need to wait or assume it is too late. Even if your concussion occurred months ago, a structured assessment evaluates your neck mobility, vestibular balance, and visual tracking to find and resolve the lingering drivers of your headaches and brain fog.
faqs.question: What If My Concussion Happened Months Ago?
